# A11Y Focus Ring & Contrast Fixes Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Fix WCAG 2.1 AA keyboard-accessibility and color-contrast failures identified in the 2026-06-18 visual audit.

**Architecture:** All fixes are pure CSS/SCSS changes in the existing partial files (`_mixins.scss`, `_layout.scss`). No PHP, no JS, no new files. The compiled output is `style.css` generated by `npm run build`.

**Tech Stack:** SCSS (compiled via `@wordpress/scripts`/webpack), Bootstrap 5 for the navbar.

## Global Constraints

- PHP 8.1+, WordPress 6.5+
- Do not alter scoring, CPT relationships, or PHP logic — CSS-only changes
- Run `npm run buildquick` after each task to compile SCSS
- Run `npm run lint:css` before committing
- `$lwtv-pink: #cb3e85` is the brand focus-ring color
- All color hex values must be WCAG AA compliant (≥4.5:1 for normal text, ≥3:1 for large/bold text)

## Out of Scope (not code changes)

- **MailerLite shortcode not rendering** — plugin/widget configuration issue, not a theme code defect.
- **Hero collage images needing `alt=""`** — those `<img>` elements are inside Gutenberg page content; fix them in the WordPress editor, not in theme files.
- **"Go" button / "New Posts" h2 / logo contrast** — all technically pass 4.5:1 today; flagged for awareness but not requiring a code change now.

### Task 1: Fix skip-link visibility on keyboard focus

**Files:**
- Modify: `scss/partials/_mixins.scss:237`

**Problem:** The `@mixin screen-reader` (line 224) applies `&:focus` to reveal the link, but `.screen-reader-text` is a `<div>` — the browser never fires `:focus` on it. Keyboard focus lands on the child `<a>`, which triggers `:focus-within` on the parent div. The reveal block never fires, so the skip link stays clipped at `height: 1px; overflow: hidden`.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `@mixin screen-reader` (used by `.screen-reader-text` in `_layout.scss:127`)
- Produces: visible skip-link pop-in on keyboard focus

- [ ] **Step 1: Read the mixin to confirm current state**

Open `scss/partials/_mixins.scss` lines 224–253. Confirm `&:focus {` starts at line 237 and closes at line 252.

- [ ] **Step 2: Add `:focus-within` alongside `:focus`**

In `scss/partials/_mixins.scss`, change:

```scss
	&:focus {
		background-color: #eee;
		clip: auto !important;
		clip-path: none;
		color: #444;
		display: block;
		font-size: 1em;
		height: auto;
		left: 5px;
		line-height: normal;
		padding: 15px 23px 14px;
		text-decoration: none;
		top: 5px;
		width: auto;
		z-index: 100000; /* Above WP toolbar. */
	}
```

to:

```scss
	&:focus,
	&:focus-within {
		background-color: #eee;
		clip: auto !important;
		clip-path: none;
		color: #444;
		display: block;
		font-size: 1em;
		height: auto;
		left: 5px;
		line-height: normal;
		padding: 15px 23px 14px;
		text-decoration: none;
		top: 5px;
		width: auto;
		z-index: 100000; /* Above WP toolbar. */
	}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Compile and verify**

```bash
npm run buildquick
```

Expected: no errors. Open the local dev URL, tab to the first element, confirm the "Skip to Main Content" link pops into view.

- [ ] **Step 4: Lint**

```bash
npm run lint:css
```

Expected: no new errors.

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add scss/partials/_mixins.scss
git commit -m "fix(a11y): reveal skip link on :focus-within so keyboard users see it"
```

### Task 2: Restore focus rings on navbar links and buttons

**Files:**
- Modify: `scss/_layout.scss:420–427`

**Problem:** The existing `.nav-link:focus` rule (line 420) only changes `background-color`. Bootstrap 5 suppresses browser-default outline on `.nav-link` via its own focus-ring variable system. Keyboard users get no visible cue on 46 of 48 nav elements (ARTICLES link, Search trigger, Dark Mode button).

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `colors.$lwtv-pink` (`#cb3e85`) from `scss/partials/_colors.scss`
- Produces: 3px pink outline on all focused navbar interactive elements

- [ ] **Step 1: Locate the nav-link focus block**

Read `scss/_layout.scss` around line 420. Confirm this block exists inside `.dark-mode-toggle` or directly in the nav section:

```scss
		.nav-link:focus,
		.nav-link:hover {
			background-color: colors.$lwtv-pink;

			svg * {
				fill: colors.$lwtv-ltgrey;
			}
		}
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Add `:focus-visible` outline rules after that block**

After the closing `}` of `.nav-link:focus, .nav-link:hover { ... }` (currently line 427), insert:

```scss
		.nav-link:focus-visible,
		.navbar a:focus-visible,
		.navbar button:focus-visible {
			outline: 3px solid colors.$lwtv-pink;
			outline-offset: 3px;
		}
```

> Why after, not merged: the hover state intentionally changes background without an outline. Focus-visible is a separate concern and should not inherit hover's `svg *` override.

- [ ] **Step 3: Add outline-offset to navbar-brand and dropdown-toggle**

The `.navbar-brand` and `.dropdown-toggle` receive the browser-default thin blue hairline, and the SHOWS dropdown toggle is clipped by the nav container's overflow. In the `#masthead .navbar-brand` block (around line 314), add a `:focus-visible` rule:

```scss
	.navbar-brand {

		@include fonts.font-26;
		font-weight: 600;
		color: colors.$lwtv-pink;

		img {
			height: 40px;
			width: auto;
		}

		&:focus-visible {
			outline: 3px solid colors.$lwtv-pink;
			outline-offset: 4px;
		}
	}
```

Then add a global dropdown-toggle rule at the end of the `#masthead` block:

```scss
	.dropdown-toggle:focus-visible {
		outline: 3px solid colors.$lwtv-pink;
		outline-offset: 4px;
	}
```

> `outline-offset: 4px` pushes the ring outside the element's painted border, reducing the chance it's clipped by an ancestor's overflow boundary.

- [ ] **Step 4: Compile and verify**

```bash
npm run buildquick
```

Tab through the navbar in a browser. Confirm a pink 3px outline appears on ARTICLES, the search icon, and the dark-mode toggle. Confirm the logo and SHOWS dropdown also show a ring.

- [ ] **Step 5: Lint**

```bash
npm run lint:css
```

Expected: no new errors.

- [ ] **Step 6: Commit**

```bash
git add scss/_layout.scss
git commit -m "fix(a11y): add :focus-visible outlines to all navbar interactive elements"
```

### Task 3: Darken Bootstrap badge backgrounds for contrast breathing room

**Files:**
- Modify: `scss/_layout.scss` (after the `.text-bg-primary` block, around line 121)

**Problem:** The stat-count badges ("7100 Characters", "2217 Shows", "622 Dead Queers") use Bootstrap 5's default `.text-bg-success` (`#198754`, ratio 4.53:1) and `.text-bg-danger` (`#dc3545`, ratio 4.53:1 — both pass by only 0.03). A slight rendering difference or darkened display pushes them below the 4.5:1 threshold. The existing `.text-bg-primary` block in `_layout.scss` shows the established pattern for overriding Bootstrap badge colors.

**Target contrast ratios:**
- Green badges → `#16704a` (≈5.8:1 vs white)
- Red badge → `#b5283c` (≈5.9:1 vs white)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: nothing (standalone overrides following `.text-bg-primary` pattern)
- Produces: `.text-bg-success` and `.text-bg-danger` with darker backgrounds

- [ ] **Step 1: Confirm the `.text-bg-primary` block ends at line 121**

Read `scss/_layout.scss` lines 100–130 to verify closing `}` is at or near line 121.

- [ ] **Step 2: Add success and danger overrides after `.text-bg-primary`**

Insert immediately after the closing `}` of `.text-bg-primary` (after line 121):

```scss
.text-bg-success {

	&,
	&:visited {
		background-color: #16704a !important;
		border-color: #16704a !important;
	}
}

.text-bg-danger {

	&,
	&:visited {
		background-color: #b5283c !important;
		border-color: #b5283c !important;
	}
}
```

> These are intentionally minimal — no hover/focus overrides needed since badge links already handle that via Bootstrap's utility framework. Extend if badges ever become interactive.

- [ ] **Step 3: Compile and verify**

```bash
npm run buildquick
```

Check the homepage badges. Confirm green badges are visibly darker and red badge is a deep crimson, not the bright Bootstrap red.

- [ ] **Step 4: Lint**

```bash
npm run lint:css
```

Expected: no new errors.

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add scss/_layout.scss
git commit -m "fix(a11y): darken text-bg-success and text-bg-danger for WCAG AA contrast breathing room"
```

### Task 4: Add consistent text-overlay scrim behind hero jumbotron text

**Files:**
- Modify: `scss/_layout.scss:265–282` (the `.jumbotron.jumbotron-fluid` block)

**Problem:** The homepage jumbotron in `header.php` sets `background-image` from the WordPress header image. White heading text achieves ~12.6:1 where the photo is darkest, but lighter portions of the collage drop contrast significantly. The audit observed no guaranteed scrim.

**Context:** The jumbotron markup in `header.php:55–66` puts the text in `.col-sm-9`. The `background-image` is on `.jumbotron.jumbotron-fluid` itself.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: none
- Produces: a consistent dark overlay behind the `.col-sm-9` text column

- [ ] **Step 1: Read the jumbotron block**

Read `scss/_layout.scss` lines 264–282 to confirm current contents:

```scss
.jumbotron.jumbotron-fluid {
	background-size: contain;
	color: colors.$white;
	...
}
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Add scrim to the text column**

Inside `.jumbotron.jumbotron-fluid { }`, add a `.col-sm-9` rule that applies the scrim:

```scss
.jumbotron.jumbotron-fluid {
	background-size: contain;
	color: colors.$white;

	@include fonts.font-18;
	margin-bottom: 0;
	max-height: 600px;

	.col-sm-9 {
		background-color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.55);
		border-radius: 0.375rem;
		padding: 1rem 1.5rem;
	}

	h1.site-description {

		@include fonts.font-40;
	}

	a.badge,
	a.badge:visited {
		color: colors.$white !important;
	}
}
```

> `rgba(0,0,0,0.55)` gives a ~12:1 contrast floor for white text regardless of the photo behind it (recommended value from the audit). The `border-radius` softens the box, matching Bootstrap's card aesthetic.

- [ ] **Step 3: Compile and verify**

```bash
npm run buildquick
```

View the homepage. Confirm the text column has a semi-transparent dark backing and text remains clearly readable across different header images. Verify no layout breakage on mobile by resizing the viewport.

- [ ] **Step 4: Lint**

```bash
npm run lint:css
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add scss/_layout.scss
git commit -m "fix(a11y): add dark scrim behind jumbotron text column for consistent contrast over header image"
```

## What this plan does NOT fix (and why)

| Audit item | Reason excluded |
|---|---|
| MailerLite shortcode renders as raw text | Plugin/widget issue — check if the footer widget is a Classic Text widget (shortcodes require `do_shortcode` filter) vs. a Block. Fix in WP Admin widget settings. |
| Hero collage `<img>` alt attributes | Those `<img>` elements are inside Gutenberg page content. Edit the block in WP Admin → Pages → Home to set `alt=""` on each decorative image. |
| Logo, "Go" button, "New Posts" h2 contrast | All technically pass 4.5:1 today. Document as known borderline values; address if the color palette is ever revisited. |
